external_entities.name: Untrusted Input Source
external_entities.description: External source of potentially malformed or malicious hex strings

ambiguities.text: No explicit error handling is documented for invalid hex characters or malformed input
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume Python's int() and Bytes.fromhex() raise ValueError for invalid hex, but caller must handle. This is a potential security concern at trust boundaries.

ambiguities.text: The specification assumes 'valid hexadecimal input strings' without defining validation criteria
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume valid means: only characters 0-9, a-f, A-F after optional 0x prefix. No length limits explicitly defined.

implicit_assumptions.description: Input strings are assumed to contain only valid hexadecimal characters
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Invalid characters could cause runtime exceptions that may not be properly handled, leading to denial of service

implicit_assumptions.description: Python's int() function correctly parses base-16 values without overflow for arbitrarily large inputs
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Extremely large hex values could cause memory exhaustion or unexpected behavior in type wrappers

implicit_assumptions.description: The type wrappers (U8, U64, U256, Uint) enforce their own bounds checking after conversion
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Values exceeding type bounds could wrap around or cause undefined behavior in cryptographic operations
